questions.question_text: What is the Perceptron Convergence Theorem, and what are its implications for single-layer perceptrons?
questions.answer_key: The Perceptron Convergence Theorem states that a single-layer perceptron can converge to a solution if the data is linearly separable. This implies that the perceptron can learn to classify data into two classes if the classes are separable by a hyperplane. (Source: CSE Scheme and Syllabus 7th _ 8th _1_.pdf, page 28)

questions.question_text: Describe the difference between a biological neuron and an artificial neuron in the context of neural network architectures.
questions.answer_key: A biological neuron is a living cell that processes and transmits information, whereas an artificial neuron is a mathematical model that mimics the behavior of a biological neuron in a neural network. (Source: CSE Scheme and Syllabus 7th _ 8th _1_.pdf, page 28)

questions.question_text: Apply the concept of the Perceptron Convergence Theorem to a scenario where you have a dataset that is not linearly separable. How would you modify the perceptron to handle this scenario?
questions.answer_key: To handle a dataset that is not linearly separable, you could modify the perceptron by adding more layers, creating a multilayer perceptron (MLP). This would allow the model to learn more complex relationships between the inputs and outputs. (Source: CSE Scheme and Syllabus 7th _ 8th _1_.pdf, page 28)

questions.question_text: What are the limitations of a single-layer perceptron, and how do multilayer perceptrons (MLPs) address these limitations?
questions.answer_key: A single-layer perceptron is limited by its inability to learn complex relationships between inputs and outputs. Multilayer perceptrons (MLPs) address this limitation by adding more layers, allowing the model to learn more complex relationships. (Source: CSE Scheme and Syllabus 7th _ 8th _1_.pdf, page 28)

questions.question_text: Describe the concept of backpropagation learning in the context of neural networks, and how it is used for efficient training of deep neural networks.
questions.answer_key: Backpropagation learning is an algorithm used for training neural networks. It involves propagating the error backwards through the network, adjusting the weights and biases to minimize the error. This is used for efficient training of deep neural networks. (Source: CSE Scheme and Syllabus 7th _ 8th _1_.pdf, page 27)
